findings.text: The reviewed run's manifest records baseline_suite: null and after_suite: null (confirmed in the run's classification.json manifest block), and its tests: field embeds the literal placeholder '<the 5 driver paths>' rather than the command that ran. So the node's 'zero added failures against the base' claim is not carried as a readable suite arm in its own record; it is substantiable only by rerunning both arms, which I did (11 passed / 0 failures at both base 68762d3639 and head eec8d3078). The sibling scanner node had recorded real arms, so this is a record-keeping regression, not a code defect - but a merge-time durability check looking for this node's after-arm would find none.

The 10 repaired sites are pinned by nothing that runs automatically. The suite arm is vacuous - grep over tests/ finds no file importing any of the five changed drivers - so tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py (11 passing) would stay green if one of the wall= arguments were removed, because that test only exercises the scanner module itself against control sites under benchmarks/. Nothing imports or invokes tests/renderer_wall_scan.py from a conftest, pytest addopts, or CI, so the only guard against a future un-masking of these sites is a manual scanner run. A later regression would not redden any automated gate.

gate_arms_note: The reviewed run recorded baseline_suite: null and after_suite: null in its manifest (confirmed in the run's classification.json manifest block), so it carries no readable JSON suite arms of its own. Its own gate logs are the scanner arms: logs/scan-base.log (base revision 68762d3639, scanner over the five driver files, 10 site records, EXIT=1) and logs/scan-head.log (head revision eec8d3078, same command, no records, EXIT=0), plus logs/test_wall_scan_head.log (uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py -q, 11 passed). I reproduced both scanner arms first-hand: at my review worktree (68762d3639, the base) the scanner printed exactly the 10 named sites and exited 1 (logs/review-scan-base.log); at the reviewed worktree (eec8d3078) the same command printed nothing and exited 0 (logs/review-scan-head.log). I also ran the only pytest suite the run touches at BOTH arms: tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py -> 11 passed, EXIT=0 at base 68762d3639 (logs/review-test-base.log) and 11 passed, EXIT=0 at head eec8d3078 (logs/review-test-head.log). after - base failure set difference = [] and added_failure_count = 0. The arm is vacuous (no test file imports any of the five changed drivers; verified by grep over tests/), which is why both arms read identically.

justifications.durability: The fix is real and pinned by a falsifiable scanner gate whose two arms I reproduced. Weaknesses, three of them. (1) The regression guard is thin: the suite arm is vacuous - no test imports any of the five changed drivers, so the existing  passing tests cannot detect a future un-masking of these sites. The only thing that would is a manual run of tests/renderer_wall_scan.py; nothing (no conftest, no pyproject addopts, no CI reference) imports or invokes it, so an edit that removes a wall= argument would not turn the suite red. (2) The guard is coupled to line numbers: the scanner's NON_RENDERER_CALLS exemptions are keyed by (path, line), and the node had to keep its edits above line 510 line-count-neutral to preserve the render_mechanism_evidence.py:510 exemption (a prior attempt shifted it to 513 and the gate reddened there). That is documented, but it means a later cosmetic edit above the exemption silently re-opens a false positive, and the coupling is not asserted anywhere. (3) The manifest records no suite arms, so the merge-time durability check has no after-arm from this node to compare against. Deductions reflect record-keeping and guard wiring, not the correctness of the mask.
justifications.evidence: Every headline reproduces first-hand. Scanner gate: base 68762d3639 -> 10 sites, EXIT=1; head eec8d3078 -> 0 sites, EXIT=0 (both rerun by me, logs on disk). The negative control is real: it is the base arm of the same command, and it lists exactly the 10 sites the fix names - I confirmed the printed site list matches the manifest's evidence_inputs line-for-line. The suite arm genuinely runs: tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py -> 11 passed EXIT=0 at both base and head. Deductions: (1) the reviewed run recorded baseline_suite: null and after_suite: null, so its manifest does not carry the zero-added-failures arm as a readable JSON arm - the claim is only substantiable because I reran both arms myself; the predecessor node on the sibling scanner review had recorded real arms, so this is a regression in record-keeping, not in the code. (2) The manifest's tests: field embeds the literal placeholder '<the 5 driver paths>' rather than the literal command that ran; the gate logs do carry the full command, so the record is recoverable but the manifest field alone is not a runnable command. (3) The node's own claim that the suite arm is vacuous is correct and I verified it: grep over tests/ finds no file importing any changed driver.
justifications.fit: Minimal and idiomatic. Ten call sites each gain the wall argument the driver already carries; no new helper, no new abstraction, no new dependency, no signature change to draw_flux_contours. The outboard-hole edit correctly prefers the unit-faithful wall_units tuple over the concatenated polyline, which matches inside_wall_units' per-unit semantics (coerce_wall_units handles a single (N,2) array, a tuple of units, or a WallUnit uniformly, so both the draw_trips single-array form and the wall_units tuple form are valid). No plan/sprint/ticket identifier in names or comments. Minor: the edit at render_mechanism_evidence.py:366 writes 'linewidth=1.4, wall=wall,' (wall after an explicit kwarg), and the wider reformatting at 511/516 expands one-line calls to multi-line, which is slightly noisy but consistent with the surrounding multi-line calls.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal - route every unguarded scattered-field renderer call in this batch through the wall mask - is met and independently reproduced. The scanner over the five named files reported exactly 10 unguarded draw_flux_contours calls at the base revision 68762d3639 and exited 1 (review-scan-base.log), and at the reviewed head eec8d3078 the same command printed nothing and exited 0 (review-scan-head.log). I read every one of the 10 edits in the commit diff and each passes the wall the driver already holds, and I confirmed each added wall variable is genuinely in scope at its call site: draw_trips.py:72 wall=np.c_[payload['wall_r_m'], payload['wall_z_m']] (line 41); direction-generators/measure.py and merit-model/measure.py pass the receipt wall; outboard-hole/measure.py:307,317 pass wall_units, the unit-faithful tuple of units from control['render_data']['wall_units_rz_m'] (line 279), NOT the concatenated wall=np.concatenate(wall_units) polyline (line 280) - the right choice, since coerce_wall_units treats a tuple of units per-unit while the concatenation merges unit boundaries; and render_mechanism_evidence.py:363,366 use the in-scope wall=record['wall'], while 868 and the _draw_error_locality pair use the local wall/record['wall']. All ten are real masks, not false guards. Not full marks only for the record-level gaps under evidence/durability.
justifications.scope_discipline: The review range 68762d3639..eec8d3078 touches exactly six paths: the five granted driver files plus the evidence fragment, all inside the run's granted write paths. No nova/ source, no plan file, no shared index, no concurrent-node path is touched. The single commit carries a conventional subject and an explanatory body; the body states what changed and why (mask to the vessel, no level array, null, caption or nova/ source changed). A scan of added lines in the changed docs/figures files finds no banned plan/stage/ticket/version label and no _v2/_new/_final suffix; the commit message carries no AI attribution trailer. The scanner stays read-only and no figure was re-rendered, as the done-when required.
